unverified: All 97 claims were found by the checker; nothing failed.
Twoubadou descent from guajira rests on English Wikipedia citing Manuel et al., Caribbean Currents p. 156; the book was not read. The page says 'guajiro traditions', not 'guitar style'.

Release years: Rezos y cantos guajiros shows release date 1957 but ℗ 1965 Ansonia; La linda guajira shows 1960 but ℗ 1997 Musart; Naborí's album is a 2012 Vintage Music reissue; the compilation tracks (Fresh Sound 2009) have no original dates. All left null.
Guantanamera written year: Spanish Wikipedia says composed 1928; English Wikipedia says radio as early as 1929 and 'consensus puts 1929'. 1928 is used; a judgement.

Peak window 1935-1965 is a judgement: the sourced start is 'around 1935' on Cuban radio; the end is chosen from Celina y Reutilio's duo (1948-1964) and Joseíto's 14-year radio programme. No source states an end.
Origin coordinates (Santa Clara, old Las Villas) are a judgement for a diffuse rural origin across western and central Cuba.
Evelio Rodríguez and Duo Spirituano are tied to the genre only by the compilation title '25 Guajiras Inmortales'; El arroyo que murmura is the 1899 first guajira by its title on English Wikipedia.

Spanish Wikipedia's API returned HTTP 429 for most of this run; pages were read from the plain article address instead. The pages for Ramón Veloz, Coralia Fernández and Radeúnda Lima were not read (missing or rate-limited).
